title: Task manager is trembling/bouncing when new apps are opened while using the reversed direction setting
line: With new tasks set to appear on the left, existing task buttons no longer jump left and slide back when a window opens.
explanation: Each task button animates moves by comparing its new x with its old x and translating the difference away. With 'new tasks appear on the left' the task list uses a mirrored layout anchored to the right, so adding a task widens the list towards the left: the list itself moves left by one button width and every existing button's x grows by the same amount while staying put on screen. The animation treated that as a move, drew each button one width to the left and slid it back. In a mirrored layout the button now tracks its distance from the list's right edge, so buttons that stay in place don't animate, while real moves (drag reordering, buttons shrinking) still do.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: don't jump task buttons when new tasks appear on the left

With new tasks on the left, the layout is mirrored and grows towards the
left, so every button's x changes when a task is added even though it
stays in place on screen. Track its distance from the right edge instead.

BUG: 499270

media.caption: Top panel task manager with new tasks on the left, one frame per row while a Konsole opens: the old Konsole button and the launchers jump one button width left over Dolphin, then slide back
Same steps with the fix: the new button appears on the left and the existing buttons stay where they are
Opening three Konsoles one after another: the buttons bounce each time
Same three Konsoles with the fix: no bounce; once the panel is full the buttons shrink and slide smoothly to the right

review.text: Tracking distance from the right edge in a mirrored layout is the right direction and stops existing buttons from jumping when opening new tasks sequentially. However, because oldX is only updated inside onXChanged, closing any non-leftmost task shrinks task.parent.width while leaving every task to its left at the same x, so their oldX goes stale and the next window open reproduces the exact jumping-left bug (and close shifts snap instead of animating). Toggling reverseMode at runtime also mixes mirrored and unmirrored coordinates in oldX, and stationary buttons still call moveAnim.restart() with a 0 delta.
changes: Keep oldX synchronized when task.parent.width changes (coalesced with x updates so two-step parent.width + x layout passes don't trigger spurious animations), so closing a non-leftmost task doesn't leave oldX stale for the next open or skip the close slide.
Reset oldX = -1 when task.parent.LayoutMirroring.enabled changes so toggling reverse mode at runtime does not mix mirrored and unmirrored coordinates.

Skip calling moveAnim.restart() when the computed delta is 0 and no move animation is running, to avoid needlessly incrementing task.parent.animationsRunning on stationary tasks, and guard task.parent against null.
Verify closing a non-leftmost task followed by opening a new task in reversed mode, as well as toggling reverse mode at runtime.
